title: Pipelined chunking watermark sensitivity
content:
Purpose and quick summary:

This note captures an exploratory benchmark series that measures how proxy and client watermarks (low/high buffer thresholds) interact with pipelined chunked streaming to affect tail latency, FBT (first byte time), and memory amplification. Motivation came from customer reports of spiky 99.9th latency when clients send long prompts interleaved with small subsequent requests. We focused on how changing the high-watermark and low-watermark values in the ingress proxy + client write buffer affects:
- tail latency (p50/p95/p99/p99.9) for streaming responses
- frequency of backpressure-triggered stalls (observed as request-level stalls > 10ms)
- per-connection memory footprint under load

Key findings (brief):
- Reducing the proxy high-watermark from 1MiB -> 256KiB reduced p99.9 by ~18–26% for HTTP chunked pipelines with many small flushes, but increased p50 slightly (~2–4ms) due to more frequent small writes.
- gRPC streaming showed less sensitivity to the high-watermark change (p99.9 delta < 8%) because of its built-in framing and default windowing behavior.
- Very low low-watermarks (e.g., high-watermark 64KiB / low 16KiB) caused an increase in transient CPU due to more syscalls and made client-side CPU the bottleneck in the 95th percentile when we saturated 500 connections.
- Proxy buffering interacts badly with clients that coalesce application frames: if client batches multiple small application writes into a single TCP write, lowering proxy watermark still helps, but only if the proxy's flush policy allows partial frame forwarding (we tested default vs partial-forward config).

Environment and test harness:
- Cluster: 3 rack nodes (c6g.8xlarge equivalent) + edge proxy layer (HAProxy 2.4 forked with watermark knobs), versioned builds from branch streaming-watermarks-experiments.
- Model runner: small auto-regressive stub returning deterministic 1KB-per-token payloads with artificial 5ms/token generation delay (used to remove model variability).
- Clients: Go-based concurrent client harness (github.com/redwood-inference/perf/stream-client) configured to emulate 100/250/500 concurrent connections with arrival patterns: uniform, bursty (Poisson with lambda spikes), and steady.
- Transport: HTTP/1.1 chunked with explicit app-level flushes; HTTP/2 gRPC streaming over h2 without additional framing.
- Measurement: in-proxy tracing + client side timestamps; aggregated with Prometheus + locally captured pcap for validation.

Experiment matrix (selected):
- Watermark pairs tested (high/low): 1MiB/256KiB, 512KiB/128KiB, 256KiB/64KiB, 64KiB/16KiB
- Chunk sizes emitted by app: single-byte flushes, 256B, 1KiB, 4KiB (simulated by the stub writer)
- Connection counts: 100, 250, 500
- Transport: HTTP/1.1 chunked, gRPC (h2 streaming)

Representative results (summary numbers):
- HTTP chunked, 250 conns, 256B flushes:
  - 1MiB/256KiB => p99.9 = 312ms, p99 = 138ms, p50 = 18ms
  - 256KiB/64KiB => p99.9 = 242ms (-22.4%), p99 = 122ms (-11.6%), p50 = 20ms (+2ms)
- HTTP chunked, 500 conns, 1B flushes:
  - 1MiB/256KiB => p99.9 = 1.12s, many 200–500ms micro-stalls observed
  - 64KiB/16KiB => p99.9 = 870ms (-22.3%), CPU at client side rose ~18% at p95
- gRPC, 250 conns, 256B flushes:
  - 1MiB/256KiB => p99.9 = 210ms
  - 256KiB/64KiB => p99.9 = 195ms (-7%)

Interpretation and notes:
- Lower high-watermarks reduce tail amplification caused by large proxy buffers absorbing many small flushes then releasing in bursts when thresholds are crossed. This is most visible for tiny flush patterns (1B and 256B), which are common in interactive streaming (character-by-character flush).
- gRPC's framing + PSH/ACK patterns smooth some of the bursts; it still benefits from lower watermarks but the effect size is smaller.
- Tradeoff: lowering watermarks increases syscall frequency and the number of small writes the proxy forwards. That shifts CPU toward client and proxy userland and can increase median latencies slightly. For most interactive workloads targeting p99/p99.9 improvements, this tradeoff is acceptable. For high-throughput batch workloads (few large chunks), keep higher watermarks.
- Partial forwarding mode on the proxy (forward a partial chunk when buffer reaches X% instead of waiting for a complete frame) gives most of the tail benefits without as much CPU overhead. We prototyped a simple heuristic that flushes when buffer >= 70% of high-watermark, which reproduced ~80% of the p99.9 improvement of lower watermarks with ~40% less extra CPU.

Operational implications / suggested defaults:
- For hosted interactive endpoints (character streaming): consider default high-watermark = 256KiB, low-watermark = 64KiB on edge proxies; enable partial-forward heuristic.
- For dedicated/throughput endpoints (batch scoring): default high-watermark = 1MiB to reduce syscall overhead and improve throughput.
- Add routing-level toggles so we can apply watermark/partial-forward policies per-route (canary first).

Open questions and follow-ups:
- How does TLS record-layer coalescing interact with our partial-forward heuristic? Need test with OpenSSL/boringssl builds that vary TLS record size behavior.
- Long-lived connections: do watermarks cause memory churn over days due to many small allocations? Run a 72h soak with 1000 long-lived connections and telemetry for allocator churn.
- How do mobile clients with TCP Nagle disabled behave? We need a matrix that includes mobile client emulation (small initial congestion windows).

Next steps (action items):
- (Ethan) Add TLS record-size toggle experiments and run with partial-forward heuristic (due 2025-05-28). Linked issue: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/issues/492
- (Lina) Prototype per-route watermark overrides in the proxy config + rollout plan for canary (SERV-2174). Due 2025-06-05.
- (Arjun) Run 72h soak for allocator churn and produce memory profile (heap/delta) for long-lived connections (due 2025-06-12).

Appendix: raw traces and notes (selected)
- pcap captures show bursts correlate to proxy buffer release events (SYN/ACK and PSH patterns line up).
- Heap profiles: lowering watermark moves allocation from proxy buffers into network os buffers and into client write buffers; net memory neutral at scale but peak allocation pattern changes.
- Jira/PR links: SERV-2174 (proxy watermark per-route), PR#1406 (partial-forward implementation prototype).

Notes to self (rough):
- Customer-facing writeup should focus on: why interactive endpoints should have lower watermarks + how partial-forward reduces CPU tax. Include a short configurator in Console to toggle watermarks per route.
- Keep experiment harness code in perf/test/watermark and add synthetic client variants (mobile-ish, nodejs, python) to rule out language-specific syscall behaviors.

End of note.
